decisions.diagnosis: On the day the counter came back from a two-day outage, southbound records isolated bursts far above anything seen before or since, most likely maintenance or testing artefacts.
decisions.evidence: Sunday total 2268 against 200-300 on normal Sundays. Single slots of 200, 411, 321, 195, 195, 184 and 122 sit next to slots of 5-17, and 411 is the site's all-time slot maximum. Northbound that day was a normal 210.

decisions.diagnosis: The northbound sensor mostly stopped detecting for 11 weeks, with an abrupt start and an abrupt full recovery, while nearby counters were normal.
decisions.evidence: Weekly northbound fell from 3700-3960 to 310-850 (about 13%), then was back at 3314 in the week of 9 Dec. The workday AM peak at 08h fell from 142 to 10 bikes/h, so the usual AM-peak shape is gone. Over the same weeks King St (568) and the Harbour Bridge (101) held steady at 4600-5500 and 7300-8500.

decisions.diagnosis: Southbound also dropped by about 45% in exactly the same window as the northbound failure, which could be partial sensor degradation or a real local diversion.
decisions.evidence: Weekly southbound fell from 4460-4800 to 1750-2720 and was back at 4313 on 9 Dec. The daily shape was kept (PM peak 94 against 158 before), and the neighbours at 568 and 101 were unchanged.

decisions.diagnosis: After the late-2014 outage the northbound channel came back almost dead, recording only a trickle, while southbound was normal.
decisions.evidence: Northbound 0-21 per day (mean about 11) with no AM peak, while southbound ran 750-930 on workdays. Northbound was back to 683-746 from 27 Apr 2015.

decisions.diagnosis: The northbound sensor failed partway through 23 Jun 2016 and recorded only a trickle for almost two years until it was repaired.
decisions.evidence: On 23 Jun 2016 northbound had 249 bikes from only 25 non-zero slots, then 4-25 per day (monthly means 8-16) through 1 Jun 2018 with about 1 bike/h all day. Southbound held its normal 409-711 per day, so the missing riders were not counted in the other direction. Northbound was 550 on 4 Jun 2018.

series.name: Northbound (Ecocounter 2012-2020)
series.evidence: The Ecocounter piezo's usable data ended in May 2020 (all zeros through Aug 2023), and the Metrocount started in Oct 2025 after a five-year gap. Against the Harbour Bridge, the new unit reads about 40% higher relative to 2019, which cannot be told apart from real growth, so the two are kept as separate series.

series.name: Southbound (Ecocounter 2012-2020)
series.evidence: Same reasoning: a five-year gap before the replacement counter, with a different vendor, so comparability cannot be checked.

series.name: Northbound (Metrocount 2025-)
series.evidence: Replacement counter from 23 Oct 2025, kept separate from the old unit because of the gap.

series.name: Southbound (Metrocount 2025-)
series.evidence: Replacement counter from 23 Oct 2025, kept separate from the old unit because of the gap.

summary: The Kent St Ecocounter's northbound channel failed repeatedly: it recorded a trickle from 10 Feb to 23 Apr 2015 and from 23 Jun 2016 to 1 Jun 2018, and about 13% of normal from 20 Sep to 8 Dec 2013 (when southbound also dropped about 45%, which is left uncertain). There was also a one-day burst of southbound artefacts on 8 Jul 2012, and the long zero outages, including the dead counter from Jun 2020 to Aug 2023, are already handled by zero_outage. The 2025 Metrocount replacement looks clean, but after a five-year gap it is kept as separate series.
